'''A & C Black''' is a British book publishing company, owned since 2000 by [[Bloomsbury Publishing]]. The company is noted for publishing ''[[Who's Who]]'' since 1849 and the ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]'' between 1827 and 1903.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Ward |first=Arthur |title=A Guide to War Publications of the First & Second World War: From Training Guides to Propaganda Posters |publisher=Pen and Sword |year=2015 |isbn=978-1-78383-154-8 |location=Barnsley, UK |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last1=Duckett |first1=Robert John |title=Know it All, Find it Fast: An A-Z Source Guide for the Enquiry Desk |last2=Walker |first2=Peter |last3=Donnelly |first3=Christinea |publisher=Facet Publishing |year=2008 |isbn=978-1-85604-652-7 |edition=3rd |location=London |pages=77 |language=en}}</ref> It offers a wide variety of books in fiction and nonfiction, and has published popular travel guides, novels, and science books.

==History==
[[File:Hall Africa 1840 UTA.jpg|thumb|[[Sidney Hall]]'s 1840 map of Africa, published by Adam and Charles Black]]
[[File:Frontispiece 1863 Woodstock-whole.png|thumb|Adam and Charles Black's 1863 edition of ''Woodstock'', by [[Walter Scott|Sir Walter Scott]] (first publ. 1826)]]The firm was founded in 1807 by Charles and [[Adam Black]] in [[Edinburgh]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1851, the company purchased the copyrights to [[Walter Scott|Sir Walter Scott]]'s ''Waverly'' novels for £27,000.<ref name=":0" /> The company moved to the [[Soho]] district of [[London]] in 1889.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Barton |first1=Susan |title=Travel and Tourism in Britain, 1700–1914 Vol 1 |last2=Brodie |first2=Allan |publisher=Routledge |year=2016 |isbn=978-1-84893-412-2 |location=Oxon |pages=25 |language=en}}</ref>

During the years 1827–1903 the firm published the seventh, eighth and ninth editions of the ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]''. This was purchased from [[Archibald Constable]] after his company's failure to publish the seventh edition of the encyclopedia.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Finkelstein |first=David |title=Edinburgh History of the Book in Scotland, Volume 4: Professionalism and Diversity 1880-2000, Volume 4 |publisher=Edinburgh University Press |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-7486-1829-3 |location=Edinburgh |pages=347 |language=en}}</ref> Adam Black retired in 1870 due to his disapproval of his sons' extravagant plans for its ninth edition.<ref name=":1" /> This edition, however, would sell half a million sets and was released in 24 volumes from 1875 to 1889.<ref name=":1" />

Beginning in 1839, the firm published a series of travel guides known as ''[[Black's Guides]]''.

The company was the publisher of the annual ''[[Who's Who (UK)|Who's Who]]'' (since 1849<ref name=":2" />) and also, since 2002, the ''[[Whitaker's Almanack]]''. Other notable works include ''[[Black's Medical Dictionary]]'' and the ''Know The Game'' series of sports rules and laws reference books.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080528000840/http://www.knowthegame.co.uk/ Know The Game], archive.org. Retrieved 16 April 2017.</ref>

The firm also published the ''A. & C. Black Colour Books: Twenty Shilling Series'' (1901–21),<ref>[http://www.publishinghistory.com/blacks-guides-adam-and-charles-black.html A. & C. Black Colour Books: Twenty Shilling Series], publishinghistory.com. Retrieved on 16 April 2017.</ref> a "range of high-quality colour collectable picture books"<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090329073834/http://www.acblack.com/aboutus.asp?mscssid=G0W21CA2GX178GM6U4GPAUXJP4GEF73F The History of A&C Black Publishers], archive.org. Retrieved on 16 April 2017.</ref> which are still collected by bibliophiles.<ref>Cliff Tomaszewski, [https://stellabooks.com/featured-book/a-c-blacks-20-colour-books "A. & C. Black's 20/- Colour Books"], Stella and Rose's Books. Retrieved 16 April 2017.</ref>

In 1902 they published [[P. G. Wodehouse]]'s first book, ''[[The Pothunters]]'', and went on to produce many of his early works.

In 1989 A & C Black purchased both Christopher Helm Publishers and later the Pica Press, publishers of the [[Helm Identification Guides]], from [[Christopher Helm]].<ref>[http://norman.hrc.utexas.edu/Watch/fob_search_results_next.cfm?FOBFirmName=C&locSTARTROW=91 FOB: Firms Out of Business], utexas.edu. Retrieved 16 April 2017.</ref>

In 2000 A & C Black was purchased by [[Bloomsbury Publishing Plc]], which continued producing the former's range of [[reference work]]s.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2013/nov/10/charles-black-obituary |title = Charles Black obituary {{!}} Publishing |work= The Guardian|date = 10 November 2013 |last1 = Gadsby |first1 = David }}</ref>

In June 2002, [[T. & A. D. Poyser]] and their back-list of around 70 [[ornithology]] titles were acquired from [[Elsevier Science]].

A & C Black purchased Methuen Drama from [[Methuen Publishing]] in 2006, and acquired [[Arden Shakespeare]] from [[Cengage Learning]] in 2008.

In 2016, A & C Black Music list moved to Collins Learning, a division of HarperCollins Publishers Ltd.
